questions.text: Why do you study or learn new things?

options.text: Because I genuinely enjoy gaining knowledge and understanding
Because it helps me get good grades or a better job

questions.text: When you complete a challenging task, what feels most rewarding?

options.text: The personal satisfaction of overcoming the challenge
The praise or recognition I receive from others

questions.text: What motivates you to work hard on a project?

options.text: My curiosity and interest in the topic
The reward or outcome I'll get at the end

questions.text: When choosing a course or subject, you prefer:

options.text: Something that fascinates me, even if it's difficult
Something that will look good on my resume

questions.text: How do you feel about homework or assignments?

options.text: I enjoy them when they help me explore ideas deeper
I do them mainly because they count towards my grade

questions.text: When you read a book, it's usually because:

options.text: I'm genuinely curious about the subject or story
It was recommended or required for a purpose

questions.text: What keeps you going when a task gets difficult?

options.text: The desire to master the skill and grow personally
The thought of the reward or avoiding negative consequences

questions.text: When you achieve something, what matters most to you?

options.text: Knowing that I've improved and grown as a person
Getting a certificate, trophy, or public acknowledgment

questions.text: You volunteer or participate in extra activities because:

options.text: It brings me joy and fulfillment
It enhances my profile and gives me an advantage

questions.text: What type of feedback motivates you most?

options.text: Understanding where I can improve and how to grow
Being told I'm the best or ranked highly

questions.text: When you set goals for yourself, they are usually about:

options.text: Personal growth, skills, or becoming better at something
Earning rewards, promotions, or external achievements

questions.text: If no one would ever know about your accomplishments, would you still pursue them?

options.text: Yes, because the journey and growth matter to me
Probably not as much — recognition motivates me

questions.text: When working in a team, you feel most motivated when:

options.text: I can contribute meaningfully and learn from others
My contribution is noticed and appreciated publicly

questions.text: How do you feel about competitions?

options.text: I enjoy them for the challenge, regardless of winning
I enjoy them mainly when I have a chance to win

questions.text: Your ideal job would be one that:

options.text: Aligns with my passion, even if the pay is average
Pays well and has great perks, even if it's not my passion

bands.label: Primarily Intrinsically Motivated
bands.text: You are primarily Intrinsically Motivated! You are driven by internal satisfaction, curiosity, and the joy of learning itself. You find fulfillment in personal growth, mastery, and doing things because they genuinely interest you. This is a powerful trait — intrinsic motivation leads to deeper learning, greater creativity, and long-term persistence.

bands.label: Primarily Extrinsically Motivated
bands.text: You are primarily Extrinsically Motivated! You are driven by external rewards such as grades, recognition, career advancement, and social approval. While this can be very effective for achieving tangible goals, consider nurturing your inner curiosity as well. Finding personal meaning in what you do can make the journey more enjoyable and sustainable.

bands.label: Balanced Motivation
bands.text: You have a Balanced Motivation style! You are driven by both internal satisfaction and external rewards. This balance means you can enjoy the process of learning while also being motivated by tangible outcomes. This adaptability serves you well in different situations.
